title: Rapid Encapsulation of Reconstituted Cytoskeleton Inside Giant Unilamellar Vesicles
protocol: Prepare 0.5 mL of chloroform in a 15 mL glass vial.
Add 88 µL of 25 mg/mL dioleoyl-phosphocholine (DOPC) to the vial.
Add 9.3 µL of 50 mg/mL cholesterol to the vial.
Add 5 µL of 1 mg/mL dioleoyl-phosphoethanolamine-lissamine rhodamine B (rhodamine PE) to the vial.
Pipette 7.2 mL of silicone oil into a second 15 mL vial.
Pipette 1.8 mL of mineral oil into the second 15 mL vial.
Mix the oils by vortexing at 3200 rpm for 10 seconds.
Add the mixture to the vial containing the lipid-in-chloroform mixture and immediately place it on the vortex mixer.
Vortex the combined mixture at 3200 rpm for 10-15 seconds.
Place the lipid-in-oil dispersion in a bath sonicator with ultrasonic power of 80 W and operating frequency of 40 kHz at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Use the mixture immediately or store it at 4 °C for up to 24 hours.
Mount the 3D-printed shaft made from black resin on the benchtop stir plate and set rotational speed to 1200 rpm.
Mount the 3D-printed cDICE chamber made from clear resin on the shaft.
Prepare actin solutions separately in a total volume of 20 µL.
Prepare actin at concentrations of 1-10 µM in globular actin buffer (G-buffer) including 10% ATTO 488 actin.
Add filamentous actin polymerization buffer (F-buffer) to the actin solution on ice to initiate actin polymerization.
Keep the solutions on ice to slow down actin polymerization before adding a crosslinker.
Wait for 15 min on ice to allow actin polymerization before adding crosslinkers.
Prepare actin-binding proteins (ABPs) separately in a microtube.
Aliquot 1.57 μl of fascin from a 1.75 mg/ml stock and add directly to the actin solution.
Add 7.5% density gradient medium into the actin solution for sedimentation facilitation.
Dispense 700 μl of outer solution containing 200 mM glucose into the chamber.
Prepare a 200 mM glucose solution as the outer solution.
Add more than 3 mL of lipid-oil mixture into the chamber until it is 60%-80% filled.
Transfer ABPs into the actin solution.
Pipette up and down 8 times with 700 µL of lipid-oil mixture added to the actin-ABP mixture.
Immediately dispense the entire emulsion into the rotating chamber.
Remove the chamber from the stir plate.
Tilt the chamber in a waste container to drain most of the lipid-oil mixture through the large opening at the center.
Hold the chamber with its lid facing towards the user.
Open the chamber lid and slightly tilt the chamber towards the user.
Collect enough outer solution containing GUVs using a pipette.
Dispense 50-300 µL of the collected outer solution into a 96-well plate.
Set up the 96 well plate on the stage of an inverted microscope equipped with a spinning disk or laser scanning confocal unit, EMCCD or sCMOS camera, and a 60x oil immersion objective lens.
Focus on any region of interest (ROI) and take a z-stack image sequence from the ROI with a z-step interval of 0.5 µm.
Capture multi-wavelength images at each z-plane if multiple fluorophores are being imaged.
Save each z-stack image sequence in .tiff format.
Open an image sequence of interest in ImageJ/Fiji.
Identify the image with the highest intensity.
Hold "ctrl+shift+c" to open the Brightness & Contrast window and click on Reset.
From the ImageJ/Fiji menu, go to Analyze > Set Scale and enter the known physical distance and its unit for each image pixel.
From the ImageJ/Fiji menu, go to Image > Stacks > 3D project to reconstruct a 3D image from the z-stack.
Set "Projection method" as Brightness Point.
Set "Slice Spacing (µm)" as 0.5.
Checkmark Interpolate.
Use default options for the rest of the settings.
